items: The legal department does not have ____ evidence to support the claim at this stage.
Evidence is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
How ____ vendors submitted proposals before Friday's deadline?
Vendors are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The redesign did not require ____ additional research before approval.
Research is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
The supervisor interviewed ____ of the candidates recommended by the agency.
Candidates are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
There is not ____ traffic near the distribution center after 8 P.M.
Traffic is uncountable in this use, so 'much' is correct.
The conference attracted ____ overseas delegates this year.
Delegates are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The revised contract leaves the supplier with ____ flexibility in setting delivery dates.
Flexibility is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
How ____ of the invoices have already been approved for payment?
Invoices are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The technician did not need ____ assistance to install the replacement unit.
Assistance is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
The retailer opened ____ temporary counters during the holiday promotion.
Counters are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The delay caused more frustration than expected but not ____ financial loss.
Financial loss is uncountable here, so 'much' is correct.
The audit team examined ____ of the transactions processed in March.
Transactions are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The new warehouse does not provide ____ space for long-term document storage.
Space is uncountable in this use, so 'much' is correct.
How ____ appointments can the clinic schedule on Saturdays?
Appointments are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The proposal did not generate ____ enthusiasm among the board members.
Enthusiasm is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
The company retained ____ of the consultants who worked on the pilot project.
Consultants are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The customer did not provide ____ notice before changing the installation date.
Notice meaning advance warning is uncountable here, so 'much' is correct.
The manufacturer ships ____ replacement parts directly from its regional depot.
Replacement parts are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The software update does not consume ____ memory on newer devices.
Memory is uncountable in this use, so 'much' is correct.
The director personally reviewed ____ of the complaints received last quarter.
Complaints are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
There was not ____ demand for the evening workshop, so it was canceled.
Demand is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
The project involved ____ subcontractors from different engineering firms.
Subcontractors are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The department cannot devote ____ attention to low-priority requests this week.
Attention is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
How ____ of the machines require calibration before the next production run?
Machines are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The finance team did not spend ____ money on outside consulting services.
Money is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
